version.changelog:
- Added built-in Python client (`scripts/kandinsky.py`) for streamlined API usage, supporting both library and CLI modes.
- Updated documentation to recommend using the Python client over manual curl calls.
- Listed `python3` as a required binary for the skill.
- No changes to the core API endpoints or functionality.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a media-generation API client, but the reported use of bearer tokens and user media over insecure HTTP needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Sending prompts, images, and audio to an external API is coherent with a Kandinsky-style media generation skill, but it involves sensitive user content and credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The supplied scan context indicates the skill does not clearly warn users at the point of use before uploading local media and prompts to the configured service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency, or package-install behavior was provided that suggests hidden execution or unrelated setup activity.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Bearer-authenticated requests to a remote API are purpose-aligned, but using plain HTTP would be disproportionate for credentials and media because it exposes them to network interception or tampering.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, privilege escalation, destructive action, or broad local indexing was identified from the available context; the main issue is network handling of credentials and uploaded content.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm the API endpoint uses HTTPS, understand which prompts and local media files will be uploaded, and avoid sending private images, audio, or secrets unless the destination service and token handling are acceptable.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The concern about bearer-authenticated API calls over plain HTTP is material if the artifact does use an http:// remote base URL, because credentials and user media should normally be sent over HTTPS.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading selected image or audio files can be expected for a media-generation client, but the available context supports a review concern because user-facing disclosure and consent appear under-scoped.
